title: GMP seeks emergency government help amid £10m budget black hole
excerpt: Greater Manchester Police (GMP) has applied for ‘exceptional financial support’ from the government amid major funding problems.
content:
Greater Manchester Police (GMP) has applied for ‘exceptional financial support’ from the government amid major funding problems.

Kate Green, Greater Manchester’s deputy mayor, said on Monday (November 16) that GMP’s application for support has not yet received a decision, and that Bev Craig is planning to meet Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood in the next few weeks.

A report in September revealed GMP was facing a budget overspend predicted to hit nearly £10m this year.

A document published by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) this week stated: ‘In 2026/27 GMP received an increase in Police Grant funding of 2.6 per cent, the second lowest increase nationally and compared to a national average increase of 3.2pc and increases of 4pc in London, 4.2pc in Kent and 3.6pc in Merseyside.’

Sir Stephen Watson, Chief Constable of Greater Manchester Police, said: “GMP is well led, well managed and full of determined public servants. Whilst there are many areas in which we seek to continue to improve, the force is currently performing well and is in a strong position.

“What is important however, is that GMP’s long-term success is not impacted by a failure to recognise that the structured funding requirement of the force is increasing in line with the growth and prominence of Greater Manchester.

“This is not to suggest that GMP’s performance is in any danger of declining in the short term. Our request for a review of the wider funding settlement merely recognises the growing pressures of the coming years.”

Mayor of Greater Manchester Bev Craig said: “It’s widely recognised that GMP are facing exceptional pressures as Greater Manchester grows. Last year we raised real concerns with ministers over the police funding settlement, which was one of the weakest in the country, and the pressure on GMP has only grown since then.

“With extra policing and security required for No 10 North, increasing pressure from national protests and more high-level events coming to the city-region, the clear imbalance in national funding for police forces is now unsustainable.

“Since coming into office in August, I have been in contact with Home Office and have been clear that this issue cannot wait any longer. GMP are now one of the best performing forces in the country and crime is going down. At a time when we must do all we can to make our communities feel safer, we need the national funding formula to reflect the work they actually do.”

At Greater Manchester’s police, fire and crime panel on Monday, Stockport Councillor Dan Oliver asked whether GMP’s financial challenges could affect the police precept – the charge paid by Greater Manchester residents through their council tax bills to fund local policing.

The police precept for 2027/28 will be set early next year.

Councillor Oliver said: “It was referred to last time by the deputy mayor that GMP were applying for exceptional financial support to government, given that may have an impact on this [precept] process, do we have an outcome or indication of where that’s up to at a government level?”

Responding, deputy mayor Kate Green said: “Colleagues will recall my reporting that the mayor was very reluctant to ask residents of Greater Manchester to bear more than their fair share of the cost of policing to keep our residents safe.

“An initial meeting has taken place now with CIPFA (the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy) who are commissioned by national government to look at our financial situation, our governance, our value for money and the approach with which we manage our resources.

“We expect there will be further discussion as a result of that, we haven’t got an outcome to our application yet, the mayor expects to meet the home secretary in the next couple of weeks and we will be putting this issue on the agenda.

“It remains our firm view that the issue GMP faces in relation to its funding is not poor financial management it is a funding formula that disadvantages metropolitan police forces, and I know the mayor is keen to make that point forcefully to the home secretary, as she has already in writing, to do so again when she meets her.”

September’s report on GMP’s finances revealed the force is taking steps to try and balance the books including making savings and introducing ‘workforce controls’.

Kate Green added in September that Andy Burnham opening Number 10 North in Manchester has piled ‘significant additional demands’ on Greater Manchester Police among other pressures on the force.

A Greater Manchester Police spokesperson said: “Greater Manchester Police is in the unique position of policing what is in effect, the second capital city of the country, with the resulting demand some other forces outside of London do not experience.

“This is further exacerbated by, in our opinion, an outdated funding formula, which leads to an over-reliance on the council tax base of Greater Manchester, which has previously allowed us to create a 3.9 per cent increase in funding. This is below the national average of 4.5 per cent and led GMP to receive the second lowest funding settlement in England and Wales.

“Despite this, GMP remains one of the best performing forces in the country, so we are confident this has not impacted on an operational level. Officers and staff continue to deliver the best possible performance they can, in spite of the extra pressures placed on them, as the force deals with increased demand due to the levels of regional and national focus it receives, without any additional government funding.

“The force can demonstrate strong financial management over the past five years, and has a strong plan for the future, but the force remains in a uniquely challenging operating environment and as such a request has been made to the government for financial support which recognises this.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “Since the election, we have increased funding to policing by £2 billion. Police force funding this year is at a historic high of £18.5 billion.

“We have established the Financial Resilience Framework to ensure a consistent approach to assessing financial resilience in policing.
“We are also reviewing the police funding formula to ensure the system is fair and continues to prioritise public safety. The new approach to funding will be brought in as part of our reforms to police structures.”
